overall: The AG found the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law on any of four allegations: notice specificity, executive session purpose and notification, and compliance with the prior order OML 2013-14.

allegations.summary: Notices for the March 5 and March 12, 2013 meetings allegedly did not list topics specifically enough to inform the public.
allegations.key_passage: the topic was sufficiently specific to inform the public that the Board would be discussing a letter from the Attorney General resolving several Open Meeting Law complaints.

allegations.summary: Chair allegedly did not give sufficient detail on the purpose for entering executive session at the March 5 and March 12, 2013 meetings.
allegations.key_passage: We therefore find that the Board met its obligation in stating the purpose for the executive session, and stating all subjects that may be revealed without compromising the purpose for which the executive session was called.

allegations.summary: Board allegedly failed to notify the individuals who were the subject of the March 12, 2013 executive session discussion.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the Board properly notified the individual who was the subject of the executive session discussion.

allegations.summary: Board allegedly failed to comply with the order in prior determination OML 2013-14 (review of the Guide and revision of March 2012 executive session minutes).
allegations.key_passage: we reviewed the revised minutes of the Board's March 8, 2012 executive session and find that the Board complied with our order.
